clue.text: He understands what others are thinking in spite of being pedestrian

definitions.text: He understands what others are thinking

parts.note: though means in spite of that, despite
a pedestrian is one who treads, a treader

explanation.surface: Someone dull and plodding who is nonetheless a perceptive judge of other people's minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like an adjective meaning dull; here it is a noun, someone on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader, a telepath, is credited with knowing people's unspoken ideas.

clue.text: Retreats which show there is method in hotheaded plans

parts.note: hot gives H, and 'headed' sets it at the front of what follows

indicators.note: the word in puts method inside the plans, a container instruction

parts.note: ideas are plans or schemes
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: There is method in a rash person's madness when they plan secret escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotheaded' reads as rash, but splits as hot set at the head of the rest; 'in' then puts the method inside the plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden refuges where one can withdraw are retreats.

clue.text: No good for service, being a little feminine in the group

indicators.note: the word in tells us the feminine abbreviation sits inside the group

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit
F is the short form, a little bit, of feminine

explanation.surface: A recruit rejected for military duty because of a slightly effeminate manner among the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone medically rejected for army duty is not fit to serve.

clue.text: Good-looking sailors love me

parts.note: hands are crew members, sailors on a ship
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast that the crew find the speaker irresistible.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a tennis score of nil is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome person is attractive to look at.

clue.text: Whichever way you look at it, it's bloodier

indicators.text: Whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: a word that looks the same read from either end is what this phrase describes, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A grim remark that however you view the battle, it was gorier.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more red, as with blood, is bloodier in colour.

clue.text: Being amazed, we stopped work at the beginning of the afternoon

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from afternoon

parts.note: taken as written
workers who struck stopped work, went on strike

explanation.surface: Workers walked out after lunch, to the astonishment of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order A, WE, STRUCK; 'at' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be filled with wonder is to be amazed.

clue.text: Order to prepare for publication about a hundred

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the editing word goes round the hundred

parts.note: to edit is to ready a text for print
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An instruction to get some hundred pages ready for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command.

clue.text: Signs of discontent when barbarian structures in-elude source of disease

indicators.note: include means take in, so the barbarian structures hold the source of disease inside

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders
arches are curved building structures
a germ is a microbe that causes illness

explanation.surface: Unrest as buildings of savage tribes are found to harbour infection.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunger marches were protest marches by the unemployed in 1930s Britain; 'include' puts the germ inside the barbarian's structures.
explanation.definitionFit: Protest walks by the jobless poor were demonstrations of public unrest.

clue.text: Ways in which a doubtful person goes without coarse food

indicators.note: goes without here means goes outside, so the doubtful person wraps the coarse food

parts.note: doubting Thomas, abbreviated Thos
rough fare is coarse food

explanation.surface: A sceptic who refuses plain meals.
explanation.walkthrough: THOS is an old abbreviation of Thomas, the apostle who doubted. 'Goes without' looks like doing without, but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads and streets are routes, public ways for traffic.

clue.text: Punished after nude display although not seen clearly

indicators.note: after tells us the punishment word follows the rearranged letters
a display shows things arranged anew, so the letters of nude are rearranged

parts.note: fined means punished with a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: Someone penalised for indecent exposure, although nobody saw them clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like the nude's exhibition, but signals rearranging those four letters; 'after' sets the penalty word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague or blurred in outline has no defined shape.

clue.text: Woman who is, back in hot water

indicators.note: back means read backwards, turning the whole run of hot plus water round

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the tide is the sea's water

explanation.surface: A lady who finds herself in trouble once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in hot water' suggests being in trouble again; actually H and TIDE are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and so a female person.

clue.text: Payment for Ulysses

explanation.surface: A sum paid to an Irish novel's hero, or to a Greek wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum awarded by an authority is an allowance; Ulysses S. Grant was the Civil War general and US President.

clue.text: Onlooker makes one stop and react badly

indicators.note: badly means done in a mangled way, so the letters of stop and react are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bystander who halts and responds poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, an observer rather than a participant.

clue.text: Peer in racket producing source of light

indicators.note: in means the nobleman sits inside the racket

parts.note: a ramp is old slang for a swindle or racket
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman caught up in a fraud that brings matters to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look; it is a noble. RAMP for a swindle is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp at a vehicle's back is a tail-light.

clue.text: In revision for oral might encounter a mathematical term

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of oral and might are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A student revising for a spoken exam may come across a maths word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revision' suggests exam study; it is the anagram signal on ORAL MIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the power to which a base must be raised, a standard mathematical function.

clue.text: The office needs water after the polish has been put back

indicators.note: after places the water word behind the reversed polish
put back means turned round, so the polish word is read in reverse

parts.note: to rub is to polish
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: Housekeeping in the office: water once the polish has been returned to the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality; it is the verb, and 'has been put back' reverses it before the French water follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an agency or department, a place of administration.

clue.text: Vanish, leaving a girl to talk foolishly about love

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: about means around, so the foolish-talk word encloses love

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl disappears, leaving to babble nonsense about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: When liquid turns to vapour it disappears from view.

clue.text: Run a cold mixture in a boiling vessel

indicators.note: a mixture is things stirred together, so the letters of run a cold are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to pour a chilled concoction into a hot pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture' fits the kitchen picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cooking pot set over a fire is a cauldron.

clue.text: Gains roughly about a second to hand out

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged gains goes round the second
roughly means approximately, not in exact order, so the letters of gains are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Earnings estimated in a moment, ready to be distributed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' turns GAINS into ASIGN, and 'about' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or allocate is to distribute.

clue.text: Corporal punishment a reactionary move?

explanation.surface: A question whether flogging is a step backwards politically.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping is a lash on one's back; a hostile reaction against change is a recoil.

clue.text: Give the old lady a slice of cake back: it will do her good

indicators.note: back means read backwards, turning the run of the old lady plus the cake slice

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, the old lady
a slab is a thick slice of cake

explanation.surface: Bring mother a piece of cake: it will cheer her up.
explanation.walkthrough: MA and SLAB are read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A balsam is a soothing ointment or remedy, something healing.

clue.text: Make a noise like water circulating in a net

indicators.note: in places the rearranged water inside the net

parts.note: a caul is a net, such as a hairnet or fatty membrane

indicators.note: circulating means moving around, so the letters of water are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sound like water swirling through a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' scrambles the water, and 'in' places it inside the net, a caul being an old word for a fine net.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to howl or screech, as a cat does.

clue.text: Fast runner appearing in prestige race

indicators.note: appearing in means found within the run of prestige race

explanation.surface: A speedy athlete taking part in an important event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a big cat noted for its bursts of speed.

clue.text: Bouquet for a lady

explanation.surface: Flowers given to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of blooms is the plant life of a region; also a woman's name.

clue.text: When dandies are about fifty they become failures

indicators.note: are about means surround, so the dandies enclose fifty

parts.note: fops are dandies, vain dressers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Ageing dandies lose their charm at fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows or ventures that fail are flops, damp squibs.

clue.text: Bumper number?

parts.note: in university bumps races, a rowing boat with that many oarsmen bumps the crew ahead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumper' suggests a big issue of a magazine; it is a boat in the Oxford and Cambridge bumps races, which are rowed by crews of this many.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing crew of oarsmen is named after its number of rowers.

clue.text: Deputy who could make ours great

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of ours great can be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A stand-in promising to improve our lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute who acts in someone's place.

clue.text: School-book about a suffragette possibly losing her head to become a leading politician

indicators.note: about means around, so the school-book surrounds the beheaded suffragette

parts.note: a primer is an elementary school text

indicators.note: losing her head means dropping her first letter

parts.note: a suffragette was a campaigner for women, perhaps described as a feminist

explanation.surface: A textbook about a campaigning woman who was guillotined, leading to political office.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffragettes campaigned for women's votes in early twentieth-century Britain; 'losing her head' drops the first letter, and 'about' puts the rest inside the school-book.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a government is its premier, the leading politician.
